h: Naira falls to four-month low of ₦1,376 per dollar
p: The naira has weakened to ₦1,376.58 per dollar in the official market, its lowest level since July. It closed at ₦1,363 on Wednesday and ₦1,430 on the parallel market.
body: The naira weakened against the US dollar in both the official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, amid reduced foreign exchange inflows and rising demand for dollars.

Data from the Nigerian Autonomous Foreign Exchange Market (NAFEM) showed the naira fell by ₦7.43, or 0.54%, to close at ₦1,363.23 to the dollar, from ₦1,355.80 the previous day. It also lost ground against the euro, closing at ₦1,495.60, but gained slightly against the British pound to ₦1,795.24.
On the parallel market, the naira slipped by ₦10 to trade at ₦1,430 to the dollar, while at one major bank's foreign exchange desk it closed at ₦1,368.
The fall comes a day after the naira lost about ₦25 against the dollar, and as the Central Bank of Nigeria and NNPC move to boost foreign exchange inflows.

By Thursday, 19 November, official data showed the naira had fallen further to ₦1,376.58 per dollar, its weakest level since July 2026, raising concerns about exchange rate stability ahead of the end-of-year trading season.
more: It is the weakest level since July.
It traded at ₦1,430 on the parallel market.
